deep.reconstruction:
Context: the page studies the polynomial f(x) = x^7 - 28x^4 + 280 and the curve in the x-plane on which Re(f(x)^2) = 20000, i.e. (Re f)^2 - (Im f)^2 = 20000. The constant 141,4 is a rounding of sqrt(20000) = 100*sqrt(2) = 141.42. The previous page, which carries a sketched curve with lobes and branches, may be the drawing of this curve; that link is my conjecture.

Line 1: 280 + 141.4 u + 141.4 sqrt(u^2-1) i = 0. A struck '20' is visible after the first '+'. The constant term 280 is perturbed by 141.4(u + i sqrt(u^2-1)). For real |u| >= 1 the point X = 141.4u, Y = 141.4 sqrt(u^2-1) runs over the hyperbola X^2 - Y^2 = 20000.

Line 2: 280 + x + sqrt(x^2 - 20000) i. This sets x = 141.4u and removes the factor 141.4 (struck through).

Line 3: 280 + sqrt(t^2 + 20000) + i t. The variable is changed to t = Im, with x replaced by t (corrected in the manuscript). This parametrizes the same hyperbola by its imaginary part t: real part 280 ± sqrt(t^2+20000), imaginary part t.

Line 4: x^7 - 28x^4 + 280 + sqrt(t^2+20000) + i t = 0. This is the family of 7th-degree equations whose constant term moves along the hyperbola. Equivalently, it is the curve Re(f(x)^2) = 20000, with t = ∓Im f.

Table: roots x (left) for given t (right).
- t = 0: x = 1.5451612. Check: x^7 - 28x^4 = 21.029 - 159.607 = -138.578, so f = 141.42 = sqrt(20000).
- t = 27.73434: x = 1.5419192 + 0.0875726i. My computation gives x^7 - 28x^4 = -135.8845 - 27.7346i, so f = 144.115 - 27.734i, and 144.115^2 - 27.734^2 = 20000.
- t = 138.9244: x = 1.5179979 + 0.4508398i.
- t = 460.6968 (pencil): x = 1.7071845 + 1.081660i. My computation gives Im(x^7 - 28x^4) ≈ -460.6 and Re f ≈ 482.3, against sqrt(460.7^2 + 20000) ≈ 481.9, which agrees within my rounding.
Thus Gauss traces one root of the equation continuously from the real root 1.54516 into the complex plane as t grows. This is a numerical continuation of a branch of the curve Re(f^2) = 20000.

Bottom right: an auxiliary rationalization of the square root. Put sqrt(x^2 + 20000) = x + α. Then (x+α)^2 = x^2 + 20000 gives 2αx + α^2 = 20000, so x = (20000 - α^2)/(2α). This is a rational parametrization of the hyperbola, letting one choose α and get t and sqrt(t^2+20000) without extracting roots (my interpretation of its purpose).
errors: Sign convention: the written equation x^7 - 28x^4 + 280 + sqrt(t^2+20000) + it = 0 gives f(x) = -sqrt(t^2+20000) - it. The tabulated roots instead satisfy f(x) = +sqrt(t^2+20000) - it. For example, at x = 1.5451612, f = +141.42. So the numbers lie on the other branch (Re f > 0) of Re(f^2) = 20000. Either the sign of the root is understood as ±, or the line differs from the computation. The right-hand column carries '-' marks that may express this.
141,4 is a rounding of sqrt(20000) = 141.421; in the later lines 20000 is used exactly.

No arithmetic errors detected in the two rows I fully verified (t = 0 and t = 27.73434); the last row agrees to about 3 significant figures in the real-part check, within my hand-computation accuracy.

results.what: Tracking a root of x^7 - 28x^4 + c as the constant c moves along a hyperbola, i.e. tracing the level curve Re(f(x)^2) = 20000 of f = x^7 - 28x^4 + 280 numerically
results.modern_name: Numerical continuation (homotopy path following) of polynomial roots; level curves of Re/Im of a polynomial
results.usually_credited_to: Root-path ideas go back to Gauss's own 1799/1849 proofs of the fundamental theorem of algebra; numerical homotopy continuation as a method is usually credited to 20th-century work (Lahaye 1934, Davidenko 1953, later Drexler, Garcia–Zangwill)

results.what: Rational parametrization of a hyperbola: sqrt(x^2+20000) = x + α gives x = (20000 - α^2)/(2α)
results.modern_name: Rational parametrization of a conic / Euler substitution

results.what: Numerical computation of complex roots of a 7th-degree polynomial to 7 decimals
results.modern_name: Numerical root finding for complex roots

deep.surprise_reason: These are worked numerical computations tied to Gauss's well-known geometric study of polynomial curves (the fundamental theorem of algebra proofs of 1799 and 1849). Following a root along a curve in the coefficient plane is a nice concrete example of root continuation, but it is consistent with what is known of his methods. There is no new theorem.

Im f ≈ -27.734 and (Re f)^2-(Im f)^2 ≈ 20000 (the t=27.73434 entry lies on Re(f^2)=20000)
